facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: Net debt is where this credit has changed. Total debt at carrying value rose from US$1,275.05 million at 2025-12-31 to US$1,985.43 million at 2026-09-30 and unrestricted cash fell from US$869.36 million to US$396.83 million, so net debt rose from US$405.70 million to US$1,588.60 million. Three events drove it: the Foran acquisition on 2026-04-14 brought in the Sprott Credit Facility, an equipment facility and government contribution obligations; the Senior Secured Credit Facility was drawn to US$325.0 million; and capital spending on property, plant and equipment reached US$1,210.02 million in nine months against US$425.75 million of operating cash flow, with the third-quarter release attributing most of that quarter's spending to Skouries and McIlvenna Bay. The mechanism is a build phase funded by the balance sheet, so net debt keeps rising until both projects reach commercial production, which the company expects in late fourth quarter 2026; the consequence for creditors is a leverage path that depends on project delivery. A ratio against a full year of earnings is not calculated because the 2025 annual statements are not in the files supplied. facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: Third-quarter financing events changed the funding mix. The Credit Facility was drawn by US$225.0 million in the quarter, taking nine-month drawings to US$325.0 million, and on 2026-08-12 it was amended to raise availability from US$450 million to US$600 million, extend maturity to 2029-03-01 and improve pricing and covenant terms. - High: The 2025 annual income statement and cash flow statement are not in the files supplied; the annual report file holds the cover document only. Annual and trailing-twelve-month EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and cash interest are therefore not established, leverage and net leverage are not calculable at 2025-12-31 or 2026-09-30, and interest cover is not stated for 2025-12-31. Supplying the audited 2025 statements, or the fourth-quarter 2025 results, would close it. Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 40-F_2025-12-31_ego-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, page 1; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 3 - High: No source states the legal rank of the instruments against each other, and the guarantor and collateral map is incomplete: the Senior Notes are senior unsecured and guaranteed, the Credit Facility is senior secured, the Term Facility is non-recourse and secured on the Skouries Project and the Hellas Gold operating assets, the Sprott Credit Facility is secured on the acquired Foran assets with a Company guarantee, and security for the Equipment Finance Facility, the VAT Facility and the government contribution obligations is not stated. The debt stack is therefore not established and no secured leverage or recovery view can be built; the indenture, credit agreement and Term Facility documents would close it. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 15 - Medium: Interest margins and floors are not stated for the Credit Facility, the Commercial Loan Facility, the Overrun Facility and the VAT Facility, the Credit Facility's amended pricing is described only as improved, and the euro and Canadian dollar instruments carry their carrying values in US dollars only, so instrument-level euro and Canadian dollar carrying values, the VAT Facility drawn balance and instrument-level amortisation are not established. Scheduled interest cannot be built from the ladder, which excludes it; the facility agreements would close it. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 15; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C32 - Medium: The fourth-quarter dividend declared on 2026-10-28 has a stated rate per share but no stated total, and the share count at the 2026-12-01 record date is not stated, so its amount and the pro forma net debt rest on the 2026-09-30 share count and may differ if shares are bought back or issued. Pro forma net leverage is not established because no trailing-twelve-month EBITDA exists. The record-date share count would close the amount. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 17; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 18; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C50 - Medium: The issuer's free cash flow, total cash costs, all-in sustaining costs and Adjusted EBITDA add-back definitions sit in a management discussion that is not supplied. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Eldorado is a gold, copper and base metals producer that sells gold as doré and gold, silver, lead, zinc and copper in concentrate from mines in Turkiye, Canada and Greece. Four mines produce today: Kisladag and Efemcukuru in Turkiye, the Lamaque Complex in Canada and Olympias in Greece. Skouries in Greece and McIlvenna Bay in Saskatchewan, the latter acquired with Foran on 2026-04-14, are ramping up toward commercial production expected in late fourth quarter 2026. Revenue of US$1,531.744 million for nine months came 45.20% from Canada, 36.27% from Turkiye and 18.53% from Greece. The credit linkage is that cash flow is visible only as far as the gold price and the Lamaque mine allow, and debt service on the build depends on projects that have not yet produced steady cash. facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: Eldorado is a listed Canadian company with no controlling shareholder or sponsor named in the documents, so financial policy is set by the board and management rather than an owner. Debt sits in three pools: the Skouries term debt of US$818.42 million is non-recourse to the parent and secured on the Skouries Project and the Hellas Gold operating assets, the parent holds the Senior Notes, guaranteed by four wholly-owned subsidiaries, and the Credit Facility, and the Foran debt is secured on the acquired assets with a Company guarantee. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is price-driven and cyclical. Third-quarter revenue rose 17.74% to US$511.860 million although gold produced fell 7.67%, because the realized gold price rose 22.65% to US$4,326 per ounce, and royalties rose with price to US$31.8 million in the quarter. Gold is 90.35% of contract revenue and the Lamaque mine 46.83% of quarterly revenue, so revenue is concentrated and Eldorado is a price taker with no pass-through. Concentrate is sold under offtake agreements, and the release says copper-gold concentrate markets are highly competitive, so treatment terms are a second price risk once Skouries produces. The effect on credit is that interest cover is strong at today's price but offers no visibility beyond the next price move. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Costs are mostly fixed at mine level and rise with volume handled and with royalties. Production costs rose to US$199.8 million in the third quarter from US$164.1 million, total cash costs rose to US$1,415 per ounce sold and all-in sustaining cost to US$2,050, yet the margin over sustaining cost still rose to US$2,276 per ounce. Kisladag is the weak point: lower grade and slower mining lifted its total cash cost 77.85% and its sustaining cost 83.30%, and higher-grade ore stacked on the heap leach pad will show in production only toward the end of the fourth quarter and into 2027 because of a leach cycle of about 300 days. Margins can therefore be defended against moderate volume pressure but not against a combination of falling price and rising unit cost at Kisladag. facts.label: Capital intensity and cash conversion
facts.text: EBITDA does not yet convert to free cash flow. Operating cash flow of continuing operations was US$425.747 million for nine months against US$1,210.017 million of additions to property, plant and equipment, and income taxes paid rose to US$227.796 million from US$120.136 million. Interest is being capitalized: US$57.668 million of the US$95.328 million of nine-month finance costs went into project cost, so when Skouries starts commercial production reported finance costs will rise toward the cash interest already paid even though cash interest does not change. Capital spending is committed at the projects but discretionary at the operating mines: guidance for growth capital excluding the projects is US$395 million to US$430 million and for sustaining capital US$170 million to US$190 million, and the projects' remaining capital falls away as they finish. Cash conversion therefore depends on the build ending, not on the operating base. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is price-based and gives no pricing power; position depends on cost, where Lamaque at US$1,436 per ounce of sustaining cost sits well below Kisladag at US$2,832. New entrants face high capital and permitting barriers, which Skouries shows: a project with a 2022 feasibility study reached first concentrate in September 2026 at a capital cost that rose in two revisions, so supply is slow to respond and incumbents hold their assets. There is no substitute for gold as a store of value, though copper and zinc by-products face industrial demand cycles. Buyer power is limited for doré but real for concentrate, because the company relies on a limited number of smelters and offtakers and Skouries volumes are contracted only for the next two years. Supplier power showed in the project overruns, where contractor workforce levels, temporary power generation and other execution costs raised capital, and in royalty burdens that rise with price. The credit consequence is that value accrues to cost position and execution, not to market structure. Basis: 40-F_2025-12-31_ego-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_eldoradogoldreportsfirstqu.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 7; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 18; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 19

facts.label: Macro, FX and regulation
facts.text: These factors are material for a producer in three jurisdictions with euro and Canadian dollar costs. The Turkish corporate tax rate change produced a US$47.4 million deferred tax gain in nine months, foreign exchange translation of deferred tax balances produced a US$41.5 million loss, and royalties rose to US$115.7 million from US$79.6 million with price. Euro and Canadian dollar zero-cost collars cover US$6.9 million and US$8.0 million a month, the Term Facility has swaps fixing 70% of the variable euro rate at 3.11% and 2.748% to 2032-12-31, and forward contracts deliver euros every six months to meet Term Facility repayments. Sector prices and jurisdiction taxes therefore move debt service capacity directly, while currency effects are partly hedged and mainly affect the euro project debt. facts.label: Credit-translated SWOT
facts.text: Strengths: a high gold price over sustaining cost, a low-cost anchor mine at Lamaque, liquidity that covers two years of principal, an equity-funded acquisition and independent governance. Weaknesses: unfinished projects absorbing cash, rising net debt without a full-year earnings figure, a third-year maturity concentration, repeated capital revisions and concentration in one mine and one metal. Opportunities that could improve credit: commercial production at Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, the Olympias expansion and Kisladag's higher-grade ore stacked in 2026 and 2027, and a pause in buybacks. Threats that could weaken credit: a fall in the gold price toward sustaining cost, a further overrun, Credit Facility drawings used for distributions and a failed refinancing of the 2029 maturities. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Scale and market position are average: nine-month revenue of US$1,531.744 million from four mines is mid-sized and the competitive advantage is cost at Lamaque rather than a moat. Business diversification is average because three jurisdictions are offset by 90.35% gold and a single mine at 46.83% of revenue. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because growth capital at the operating mines is discretionary while project capital is committed. Margin stability is average: the margin on metal sales was 57.04% but depends on price. Free cash flow stability is weak, with consolidated free cash flow negative US$654.3 million for nine months. Refinancing access is average, supported by the extended Credit Facility and a Senior Notes fair value of 98.38% of face value. Liquidity is adequate at US$671.53 million. Financial policy and governance are average, with distributions continuing during the build. The trend is a growing balance sheet whose debt was added ahead of the cash flow it is meant to repay, and the key missing data are trailing earnings and the debt documents. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: The next 12 to 24 months are set by commissioning. Tailwinds are first concentrate at both new mines, grid power at Skouries from 2026-09-28, the Term Facility being fully drawn so no further project debt is available, Kisladag's higher-grade ore and the realized gold price. Headwinds are the start of Term Facility repayments on 2026-12-31, with US$141.05 million of principal due within one year, higher guided capital at the operating mines, revised and lower 2026 production guidance, and capitalized interest ending as projects start, which raises reported finance costs. Over three to five years Skouries has a stated mine life of 20 years and McIlvenna Bay of 18 years on management studies, which would diversify revenue toward copper, but those are management statements and the 2029 maturities arrive within that window. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario that fits this issuer is a commissioning slip combined with a lower gold price. If Skouries or McIlvenna Bay fails to reach commercial production in the fourth quarter of 2026, project and accelerated operational capital continue beyond the estimate, free cash flow stays negative and cash falls from US$396.83 million while the Credit Facility is drawn from its US$274.7 million balance. Term Facility repayments begin on 2026-12-31 and dividends continue, so liquidity of US$671.53 million falls without the new mines' cash to replace it. A gold price fall would cut revenue directly because there is no pass-through, although the price would have to fall 52.61% to reach third-quarter sustaining cost. Management can pause buybacks and dividends, defer growth capital at the operating mines, draw the Credit Facility and sell investments. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 12 months because liquidity covers principal due 2.37x, but not to meet the 2029 maturities from liquidity alone, so refinancing capacity would decide the outcome. The observable triggers are a missed commercial production date, a further capital revision and further Credit Facility drawings. If Skouries or McIlvenna Bay fails to reach commercial production in the fourth quarter of 2026, project and accelerated operational capital continue beyond the estimate, free cash flow stays negative and cash falls from US$396.83 million while the Credit Facility is drawn from its US$274.7 million balance. Term Facility repayments begin on 2026-12-31 and dividends continue, so liquidity of US$671.53 million falls without the new mines' cash to replace it. A gold price fall would cut revenue directly because there is no pass-through, although the price would have to fall 52.61% to reach third-quarter sustaining cost. Management can pause buybacks and dividends, defer growth capital at the operating mines, draw the Credit Facility and sell investments. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 12 months because liquidity covers principal due 2.37x, but not to meet the 2029 maturities from liquidity alone, so refinancing capacity would decide the outcome. The observable triggers are a missed commercial production date, a further capital revision and further Credit Facility drawings.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 19; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 7; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C4; calculation C6

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Eldorado presents an adequate business profile supported by four producing mines, a gold price well above sustaining cost, covered cash interest and two years of liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by net debt of US$1,588.60 million that rose while two projects absorbed capital, a back-loaded maturity profile and a legal structure whose ranking is not established. Cash-flow durability appears adequate at the operating mines and weak at consolidated level until the projects produce. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on commercial production, the gold price and the Credit Facility's 2029 maturity. The primary downside path is a commissioning slip that meets the 2029 maturities with the build unfinished. Further analysis would require trailing-twelve-month earnings, the debt documents and a rating or market quote. Top risk: execution at Skouries and McIlvenna Bay. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C1; calculation C12

## Findings
### Bottom line

Eldorado's earnings cover its cash interest comfortably today, but net debt has risen from US$405.70 million at the end of 2025 to US$1,588.60 million at 2026-09-30 as Skouries and McIlvenna Bay absorb cash, so creditors are underwriting project completion.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C05; calculation C08; calculation C51

Reported EBITDA of US$873.69 million for the nine months was 11.72x cash interest paid of US$74.55 million. Liquidity is US$396.83 million of unrestricted cash plus US$274.7 million available on the Credit Facility, and a further US$71.90 million is restricted for Term Facility repayments that begin on 2026-12-31. A leverage multiple on a full year of earnings cannot be calculated because the 2025 annual statements are not in the files supplied, and no source ranks the debt instruments against each other.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C17; calculation C36; calculation C51

### Financial interpretation

Net debt is where this credit has changed. Total debt at carrying value rose from US$1,275.05 million at 2025-12-31 to US$1,985.43 million at 2026-09-30 and unrestricted cash fell from US$869.36 million to US$396.83 million, so net debt rose from US$405.70 million to US$1,588.60 million. Three events drove it: the Foran acquisition on 2026-04-14 brought in the Sprott Credit Facility, an equipment facility and government contribution obligations; the Senior Secured Credit Facility was drawn to US$325.0 million; and capital spending on property, plant and equipment reached US$1,210.02 million in nine months against US$425.75 million of operating cash flow, with the third-quarter release attributing most of that quarter's spending to Skouries and McIlvenna Bay. The mechanism is a build phase funded by the balance sheet, so net debt keeps rising until both projects reach commercial production, which the company expects in late fourth quarter 2026; the consequence for creditors is a leverage path that depends on project delivery. A ratio against a full year of earnings is not calculated because the 2025 annual statements are not in the files supplied.

Coverage is strong on the figures that exist. Nine-month reported EBITDA of US$873.69 million was 11.72x the US$74.55 million of cash interest paid, and the same ratio was 10.62x a year earlier, so cover did not deteriorate while debt rose. The cash interest figure includes US$45.94 million of capitalized interest paid in investing activities; counting only the interest expensed would have flattered the ratio. This ratio uses nine months and the report's own definitions, so it is not a test of the Credit Facility interest cover covenant, which is measured on rolling four quarters.

- Ownership gives no sponsor to assess, which removes sponsor-extraction risk but leaves control unverified. The documents name no controlling shareholder, and the only holder class identified is the former Foran shareholders, who received 24.72% of the shares in issue in April 2026; a holder with a large stake would change this finding.

- Capital allocation is the main governance risk. Dividends and share cancellations totalled US$138.00 million in nine months, 32.41% of operating cash flow of US$425.75 million, while the Credit Facility was drawn to US$325.0 million and the two new mines absorbed capital. Returns that compete with project completion delay deleveraging, and the new chief executive's stated aim to balance debt reduction, reinvestment and shareholder returns is management language with no disclosed limit.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against concern is that the operating mines fund themselves: the issuer's free cash flow excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay was US$202.1 million for nine months, the Foran deal was paid in shares, the new chief executive has put capital discipline and balance-sheet strength first, and the issuer reports compliance with every covenant at 2026-09-30. Skouries produced its first concentrate on 2026-09-08 and was connected to grid power on 2026-09-28, so the main construction milestones are behind the project, although commissioning continues. Taken together these would support a Low risk level.

The view would improve to Low if both mines reach commercial production in late fourth quarter 2026 without a further capital revision, buybacks pause while net debt is falling and dividends stay within operating cash flow. It would worsen to High if capital estimates rise again, if the Credit Facility is drawn further to fund distributions, if a large shareholder with an extraction record appears, or if executed agreements show wide capacity for restricted payments and priming.

- High: No shareholder register, insider holding or control right is supplied, so the absence of a sponsor is an absence of disclosure and not a finding that no large holder exists. spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit for ELDORADO GOLD CORP /FI as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the integrated credit view of the business, ownership, financial profile, outlook and downside, built from the seven supplied documents and the three earlier modules, with monitoring triggers and ranked drivers.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Eldorado's operating mines carry the credit today, but net debt has risen sharply as two unfinished mines absorb capital, so creditors depend on on-time commissioning and the 2029 refinancing rather than on proven leverage.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 6

Net debt was US$1,588.60 million at 2026-09-30, or US$1,608.22 million pro forma for the fourth-quarter dividend payable on 2026-12-15, an estimate on the 2026-09-30 share count; pro forma leverage is not established. Reported EBITDA of US$873.69 million for nine months was 11.72x cash interest, liquidity is US$671.53 million, and net debt is 1.82x nine-month EBITDA, which is not a leverage ratio and would be lower on a trailing year. Business quality and liquidity are adequate, free cash flow stability and leverage visibility are weak, and the top risk is a slip in commissioning that meets the 2029 maturities with the build unfinished.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 1; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C12
### Key findings

- Business quality is adequate and carried by four operating mines. Reported EBITDA margin on metal sales was 57.04% for nine months and EBITDA covered cash interest 11.72x at a realized gold price of US$4,326 per ounce, so the operating base services its debt comfortably while gold stays near today's level.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C3

- Leverage visibility is weak. Net debt rose by US$1,182.90 million in nine months to US$1,588.60 million at 2026-09-30, or US$1,608.22 million pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-12-15; no trailing-twelve-month EBITDA exists, so leverage is not calculated, and on nine months of EBITDA alone net debt is 1.82x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2

- Free cash flow stability is weak until the new mines produce. Consolidated free cash flow was negative US$654.3 million for nine months, while the issuer's measure excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay was positive US$202.1 million, so the two projects explain the gap and their delivery decides when cash flow turns.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C8

- Liquidity is adequate near term but the maturity profile is back-loaded. Liquidity of US$671.53 million covers the US$283.60 million of principal due in two years 2.37x, but US$958.80 million falls due in the third year, including US$325.0 million drawn on the Credit Facility and US$500.0 million of Senior Notes.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C4; calculation C5

- Refinancing capacity is average. The Credit Facility was enlarged and extended to 2029-03-01 and the issuer's fair value for the Senior Notes was 98.38% of face value, but no rating, market quote or peer comparison is supplied, so access to capital markets is inferred from a single disclosure.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C7

- Execution risk is the primary downside path. Skouries capital rose 22.84% in two revisions, Kisladag cost per ounce rose sharply, and guidance was cut, so a further slip would meet the third-year maturities with the build unfinished.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_eldoradogoldreportsfirstqu.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C11; calculation C10

- Concentration and shareholder returns are the governance-related constraints. Lamaque produced 46.83% of third-quarter revenue, gold was 90.35% of contract revenue, and dividends and share cancellations took US$138.00 million in nine months while net debt rose.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 19; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 15; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C11; calculation C9
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a stronger view is the cushion in the gold price. The realized price exceeded all-in sustaining cost by US$2,276 per ounce in the third quarter, so the price would have to fall 52.61% before the operating mines stopped covering sustaining cost, and the issuer's free cash flow excluding the two projects was positive US$202.1 million for nine months. Net debt is only 1.82x nine-month EBITDA, and the Foran acquisition was paid in shares. Together these argue that leverage on a full year will prove moderate once the build ends.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 13; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C2; calculation C8

The strongest evidence for a weaker view is that the cushion belongs to the operating mines while the debt belongs to the build. Project capital has risen twice, the 2026 gold guidance was cut, and the Credit Facility has absorbed the gap. The view would improve if both mines declare commercial production in the fourth quarter of 2026 and capital spending falls, if the third-quarter measures of cost per ounce hold, and if trailing-twelve-month EBITDA, once available, shows leverage well inside the Credit Facility test. It would worsen if a further capital revision, a slower ramp-up or a gold price fall toward sustaining cost arrives before the 2029 maturities, or if distributions continue while the Credit Facility is drawn further.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 7; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14
### Limitations

- Without earnings for a trailing year the leverage conclusion rests on a nine-month bound and on liquidity, so the view that leverage is moderate could be wrong in either direction once the fourth quarter of 2025 is known.

### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is a cost-advantaged operating base that converts price into cash. Lamaque earns the largest share of revenue at the lowest cost per ounce, and the realized price exceeded all-in sustaining cost by US$2,276 per ounce, which supports interest cover of 11.72x and lets the operating mines absorb a large price fall before sustaining cost is uncovered.

The second strength is near-term liquidity. Cash of US$396.83 million and US$274.7 million available on the Credit Facility give US$671.53 million against US$283.60 million of principal due in two years, so scheduled principal through 2028 does not depend on market access.

The third strength is the funding of Foran in shares and the larger, longer Credit Facility, which avoided a debt-funded acquisition and moved the parent's secured maturity to 2029-03-01. The fifth is independent governance with effective internal control and stated covenant compliance.

### Company description

Eldorado is a gold, copper and base metals producer that sells gold as doré and gold, silver, lead, zinc and copper in concentrate from mines in Turkiye, Canada and Greece. Four mines produce today: Kisladag and Efemcukuru in Turkiye, the Lamaque Complex in Canada and Olympias in Greece. Skouries in Greece and McIlvenna Bay in Saskatchewan, the latter acquired with Foran on 2026-04-14, are ramping up toward commercial production expected in late fourth quarter 2026. Revenue of US$1,531.744 million for nine months came 45.20% from Canada, 36.27% from Turkiye and 18.53% from Greece. The credit linkage is that cash flow is visible only as far as the gold price and the Lamaque mine allow, and debt service on the build depends on projects that have not yet produced steady cash.

### Ownership and group structure

Eldorado is a listed Canadian company with no controlling shareholder or sponsor named in the documents, so financial policy is set by the board and management rather than an owner. Debt sits in three pools: the Skouries term debt of US$818.42 million is non-recourse to the parent and secured on the Skouries Project and the Hellas Gold operating assets, the parent holds the Senior Notes, guaranteed by four wholly-owned subsidiaries, and the Credit Facility, and the Foran debt is secured on the acquired assets with a Company guarantee. Dividends and buybacks of US$138.00 million in nine months, a new chief executive and a new chair mean financial policy is being reset during commissioning. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk as Medium, and this module adopts that view without adding evidence.

### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is price-driven and cyclical. Third-quarter revenue rose 17.74% to US$511.860 million although gold produced fell 7.67%, because the realized gold price rose 22.65% to US$4,326 per ounce, and royalties rose with price to US$31.8 million in the quarter. Gold is 90.35% of contract revenue and the Lamaque mine 46.83% of quarterly revenue, so revenue is concentrated and Eldorado is a price taker with no pass-through. Concentrate is sold under offtake agreements, and the release says copper-gold concentrate markets are highly competitive, so treatment terms are a second price risk once Skouries produces. The effect on credit is that interest cover is strong at today's price but offers no visibility beyond the next price move.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Costs are mostly fixed at mine level and rise with volume handled and with royalties. Production costs rose to US$199.8 million in the third quarter from US$164.1 million, total cash costs rose to US$1,415 per ounce sold and all-in sustaining cost to US$2,050, yet the margin over sustaining cost still rose to US$2,276 per ounce. Kisladag is the weak point: lower grade and slower mining lifted its total cash cost 77.85% and its sustaining cost 83.30%, and higher-grade ore stacked on the heap leach pad will show in production only toward the end of the fourth quarter and into 2027 because of a leach cycle of about 300 days. Margins can therefore be defended against moderate volume pressure but not against a combination of falling price and rising unit cost at Kisladag.

### Capital intensity and cash conversion

EBITDA does not yet convert to free cash flow. Operating cash flow of continuing operations was US$425.747 million for nine months against US$1,210.017 million of additions to property, plant and equipment, and income taxes paid rose to US$227.796 million from US$120.136 million. Interest is being capitalized: US$57.668 million of the US$95.328 million of nine-month finance costs went into project cost, so when Skouries starts commercial production reported finance costs will rise toward the cash interest already paid even though cash interest does not change. Capital spending is committed at the projects but discretionary at the operating mines: guidance for growth capital excluding the projects is US$395 million to US$430 million and for sustaining capital US$170 million to US$190 million, and the projects' remaining capital falls away as they finish. Cash conversion therefore depends on the build ending, not on the operating base.

### Competitive forces

Rivalry is price-based and gives no pricing power; position depends on cost, where Lamaque at US$1,436 per ounce of sustaining cost sits well below Kisladag at US$2,832. New entrants face high capital and permitting barriers, which Skouries shows: a project with a 2022 feasibility study reached first concentrate in September 2026 at a capital cost that rose in two revisions, so supply is slow to respond and incumbents hold their assets. There is no substitute for gold as a store of value, though copper and zinc by-products face industrial demand cycles. Buyer power is limited for doré but real for concentrate, because the company relies on a limited number of smelters and offtakers and Skouries volumes are contracted only for the next two years. Supplier power showed in the project overruns, where contractor workforce levels, temporary power generation and other execution costs raised capital, and in royalty burdens that rise with price. The credit consequence is that value accrues to cost position and execution, not to market structure.

### Macro, FX and regulation

These factors are material for a producer in three jurisdictions with euro and Canadian dollar costs. The Turkish corporate tax rate change produced a US$47.4 million deferred tax gain in nine months, foreign exchange translation of deferred tax balances produced a US$41.5 million loss, and royalties rose to US$115.7 million from US$79.6 million with price. Euro and Canadian dollar zero-cost collars cover US$6.9 million and US$8.0 million a month, the Term Facility has swaps fixing 70% of the variable euro rate at 3.11% and 2.748% to 2032-12-31, and forward contracts deliver euros every six months to meet Term Facility repayments. Sector prices and jurisdiction taxes therefore move debt service capacity directly, while currency effects are partly hedged and mainly affect the euro project debt.

### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths: a high gold price over sustaining cost, a low-cost anchor mine at Lamaque, liquidity that covers two years of principal, an equity-funded acquisition and independent governance. Weaknesses: unfinished projects absorbing cash, rising net debt without a full-year earnings figure, a third-year maturity concentration, repeated capital revisions and concentration in one mine and one metal. Opportunities that could improve credit: commercial production at Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, the Olympias expansion and Kisladag's higher-grade ore stacked in 2026 and 2027, and a pause in buybacks. Threats that could weaken credit: a fall in the gold price toward sustaining cost, a further overrun, Credit Facility drawings used for distributions and a failed refinancing of the 2029 maturities.

### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position are average: nine-month revenue of US$1,531.744 million from four mines is mid-sized and the competitive advantage is cost at Lamaque rather than a moat. Business diversification is average because three jurisdictions are offset by 90.35% gold and a single mine at 46.83% of revenue. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because growth capital at the operating mines is discretionary while project capital is committed. Margin stability is average: the margin on metal sales was 57.04% but depends on price. Free cash flow stability is weak, with consolidated free cash flow negative US$654.3 million for nine months. Refinancing access is average, supported by the extended Credit Facility and a Senior Notes fair value of 98.38% of face value. Liquidity is adequate at US$671.53 million. Financial policy and governance are average, with distributions continuing during the build. The trend is a growing balance sheet whose debt was added ahead of the cash flow it is meant to repay, and the key missing data are trailing earnings and the debt documents.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

The next 12 to 24 months are set by commissioning. Tailwinds are first concentrate at both new mines, grid power at Skouries from 2026-09-28, the Term Facility being fully drawn so no further project debt is available, Kisladag's higher-grade ore and the realized gold price. Headwinds are the start of Term Facility repayments on 2026-12-31, with US$141.05 million of principal due within one year, higher guided capital at the operating mines, revised and lower 2026 production guidance, and capitalized interest ending as projects start, which raises reported finance costs. Over three to five years Skouries has a stated mine life of 20 years and McIlvenna Bay of 18 years on management studies, which would diversify revenue toward copper, but those are management statements and the 2029 maturities arrive within that window.

### Downside scenario

The scenario that fits this issuer is a commissioning slip combined with a lower gold price. If Skouries or McIlvenna Bay fails to reach commercial production in the fourth quarter of 2026, project and accelerated operational capital continue beyond the estimate, free cash flow stays negative and cash falls from US$396.83 million while the Credit Facility is drawn from its US$274.7 million balance. Term Facility repayments begin on 2026-12-31 and dividends continue, so liquidity of US$671.53 million falls without the new mines' cash to replace it. A gold price fall would cut revenue directly because there is no pass-through, although the price would have to fall 52.61% to reach third-quarter sustaining cost. Management can pause buybacks and dividends, defer growth capital at the operating mines, draw the Credit Facility and sell investments. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 12 months because liquidity covers principal due 2.37x, but not to meet the 2029 maturities from liquidity alone, so refinancing capacity would decide the outcome. The observable triggers are a missed commercial production date, a further capital revision and further Credit Facility drawings.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Eldorado presents an adequate business profile supported by four producing mines, a gold price well above sustaining cost, covered cash interest and two years of liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by net debt of US$1,588.60 million that rose while two projects absorbed capital, a back-loaded maturity profile and a legal structure whose ranking is not established. Cash-flow durability appears adequate at the operating mines and weak at consolidated level until the projects produce. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on commercial production, the gold price and the Credit Facility's 2029 maturity. The primary downside path is a commissioning slip that meets the 2029 maturities with the build unfinished. Further analysis would require trailing-twelve-month earnings, the debt documents and a rating or market quote. Top risk: execution at Skouries and McIlvenna Bay.

- High: No trailing-twelve-month EBITDA exists, because the 2025 annual statements are not supplied, so leverage and net leverage are not calculated and the leverage view rests on a nine-month bound, on interest cover and on liquidity. The audited 2025 statements or fourth-quarter 2025 results would close it.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C2

- High: No indenture, credit agreement, Term Facility or Sprott document is supplied and no source ranks the instruments, so priority, collateral, covenant headroom and capacity for distributions and debt are not established. The legal documents would close it.
